description: I’m a Chemical Engineering student at the University of Bahrain and President of the SPE UOB Student Chapter. I’m passionate about research, innovation, and solving real-world challenges. My strengths include analytical thinking, leadership, teamwork, and project management. I’m looking for creative, motivated teammates skilled in AI, programming, data analysis, and web development. Let’s combine our expertise to develop an innovative solution and make an impact!
summary:
PyroX Intelligence is an AI-powered, web-based research and decision-support dashboard developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to synthesize, rank, and interpret low-gravity combustion science investigations from NASA's Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database.

The project addresses the challenge of navigating overwhelming combustion datasets by translating complex experimental data into clear, actionable fire safety insights tailored for habitable crew environments, including spacecraft, space stations, pressurized rovers, and future lunar and Martian bases.

It is vital because microgravity and elevated oxygen concentrations—such as the 30%+ oxygen environments planned for lunar habitats—fundamentally alter combustion dynamics and dramatically increase material flammability. PyroX bridges the gap between raw experimental data and mission-critical engineering, ensuring enhanced prevention, detection, and suppression strategies to safeguard astronauts during long-duration space exploration.
details:
• What it does & How it works:
    It acts like a smart search engine for NASA's space fire experiments. Users can filter, search, and compare different tests (looking at things like fuel types, oxygen levels, and airflow) just by typing ordinary questions. An AI assistant then finds the answers and ranks which experiments matter most for keeping astronauts safe.
    • Saves hours of time by organizing messy science data.
    • Lets you compare different space fire tests side-by-side.
    • Turns complicated science facts into clear, practical advice for building safer spaceships and gear.
  • Who it is for (Intended Impact):
    It helps scientists, students, and engineers design safer habitats (like future Moon and Mars bases). It also shows how space fire safety tricks can be used to make better firefighter gear right here on Earth.
    • Website Design: Built using standard web tools (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript) to create a clean, modern dashboard.
    • Data & AI: Uses smart search technology powered by NASA's real space research guides.
    • Simulated Gear: Modeled after real NASA space station testing tools, like the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR).
  • What makes it creative:
    Instead of boring text reports, it looks and feels like a futuristic spaceship control panel. It features a side-by-side comparison tool and gives clear answers that always point back to the real NASA source.
    • Space Extremes: Looked at how dangerous high-oxygen environments (like lunar bases with 30%+ oxygen) and different air pressures change the way fires burn.
    • Earth Spinoffs: Made sure the lessons learned in space could also improve everyday fire safety tools on Earth.
